Study design
The USDM / ICH M11 design object this protocol is a projection of. The protocol document carries the registers; the design object carries the estimands, the endpoints, the statistical plan and the schedule.
Unbind study design
TD-UI-001 study design — SYNTHETIC
Phase 2 · Fictional inflammatory condition for UI testing · draft
Study design id
sd_75ad27f0add14a04a478139e78ee4c22
Bound
2026-11-14
Standards evaluated
ICH E9 §5.2, ICH E9 §5.4, ICH E9(R1), ICH E9(R1) §A.5
Design gates
The deterministic gate engine’s findings on the design object — ICH E9, E9(R1), E10 and E3, and ICH M11 §2/§3/§4/§6/§7/§10/§17. These are findings on the DESIGN, not on this document’s text.
Design is blocked: critical defensibility findings must be resolved before approval. (1 critical, 4 major, 1 minor).
Risk level
critical
Blocks approval
yes
Critical
EST-001 — No estimand for primary endpoint. Endpoint "Fictional symptom score change" has no estimand. Per ICH E9(R1) every objective must be expressed as an estimand before the analysis is finalized. (ICH E9(R1)) Fix: Define the estimand: treatment condition, population, variable, intercurrent-event strategy, and population-level summary measure.
Major
PWR-001 — No target power specified. The design does not state a target power. Fix: State target power (≥80% standard, ≥90% for confirmatory).
Major
POP-001 — No analysis populations defined. The design declares no analysis population, so the primary analysis has no defined analysis set. (ICH E9 §5.2) Fix: Define ITT (or the frame-appropriate primary set), per-protocol and safety populations, and mark the primary set.
Major
MTH-001 — No planned analysis for primary endpoint "Fictional symptom score change". The statistical plan names no analysis method for this endpoint, so its primary analysis is not pre-specified. (ICH E9 §5.4) Fix: Add a planned analysis naming the method (e.g. MMRM, Cox proportional hazards, logistic regression) and the estimand it targets.
Major
MIS-001 — No missing-data strategy specified. The statistical plan does not say how missing outcomes are handled in the primary analysis, so the estimand cannot be shown to be estimated. (ICH E9(R1) §A.5) Fix: Pre-specify the primary approach (e.g. MMRM under MAR, multiple imputation, tipping-point sensitivity) aligned with the estimand strategy.
Minor
PWR-003 — No sensitivity analysis across assumptions. Sample size rests on point assumptions with no sensitivity analysis across plausible ranges. A single-point estimate is a reviewer red-flag. Fix: Add a sensitivity analysis across effect-size and dropout ranges.
Planning inputs
The sponsor inputs the planning projections read. Each is a governed write to the design object, with a reason; nothing here is computed or assumed.

Master protocol structure
ICH M11 protocol — A projection of the study design object as an ICH M11-structured protocol.
Statistical Analysis Plan skeleton — A projection of the study design object’s statistical plan and estimands (ICH E9 / E9(R1)).
Schedule of Activities — A projection of the study design object’s time-and-events grid (ICH M11 §1.3).
Trial registry record — A projection of the study design object as a registry record — ClinicalTrials.gov under FDAAA 801 and EU CTIS under Regulation 536/2014.
CRF shell — A projection of the study design object’s Schedule of Activities as a blank CRF set (CDISC CDASH).
Trial schema — A projection of the study design object as the ICH M11 §1.2 trial schema — epochs, randomisation, arms.
SPIRIT 2013 checklist — The study design object judged against the SPIRIT 2013 checklist, row by row — a checklist since superseded by SPIRIT 2025. Rows only a protocol section can evidence are not assessable from the design alone.
Critical-to-quality factors — Critical-to-quality factors (ICH E6(R3)) derived from the study design object, each with the design element it came from. Ratings are default seeds.
USDM export — The study design object as a CDISC USDM-shaped object graph. Conformance is unverified: the USDM schema is not vendored, so nothing has been validated against it.
Decentralised elements — Where each Schedule of Activities activity happens, per the FDA decentralized-elements guidance. An activity with no stated location is unstated — not assumed to be at the site.
WHO registration data set — The study design object as the WHO Trial Registration Data Set (24 items). Sponsor, contacts, dates, ethics and results are supplied at registration, not by the design.
Dose escalation (BOIN) — The study design object’s dose-escalation rules, computed by the BOIN engine (Liu & Yuan 2015). A value marked engine default was not chosen by the sponsor.
Enrollment forecast — Time to the planned sample size from the sponsor’s site accrual plan, by the Poisson–Gamma engine. Site rates are sponsor inputs; none is assumed.
Interim analysis characteristics — Type I error, power and expected sample size of the study design object’s interim plan, computed exactly. A recorded boundary that departs from the spending function is shown as a discrepancy.
MMRM sample size — The sample size the MMRM-analysed endpoint needs under the sponsor’s recorded assumptions, checked against the planned N. No assumption is supplied when one is missing.
External-control plan — What the study design object pre-specifies about borrowing from an external control, and how strongly it borrows (FDA 2023 draft guidance).
Multiplicity control — Whether the study design object’s multiplicity procedure holds the family-wise error at alpha over its confirmatory endpoints, by seeded simulation.
Specimens and blood volume — What the Schedule of Activities collects, what the lab manual still needs, and how much blood a participant gives. Reference points are expedited-review thresholds, not safety limits.
Master protocol structure — For a platform, basket, umbrella or MAMS design: what the plan states per sub-study and across them, against FDA’s master-protocol guidances.
